div.head: II As 26
div.ab: Ond se ðe manað swerige, ⁊ hit him on open wurþe, ðæt he næfre eft aðwyrþe ne sy, ne binnon nanum gehalgodum lictune ne licge, þeah he forðfore, buton he hæbbe ðæs biscopes gewitnesse, ðe he on his scriftscire sy, þæt he hit swa gebet hæbbe, swa him his scrift scrife.

Be mansworum. Se ðe mænne aþ swerige, ⁊ hit him on open weorþe, þæt he næfre aþwyrþe ne sy, ne binnan nanum gehalgodum lictune ne licge, ðeah he gefære, butan he hæbbe ðæs bisceopes gewitnysse, ðe he on his scire sy, þæt he hit swa gebete hæbbe, swa his scrift him scrife.

De omnibus periuris. Qui falsum iuramentum iurauerit et conuictus inde fuerit, numquam postea iuramento dignus sit nec in sanctificato atrio aliquo iaceat, si moriatur, nisi (si non) habeat episcopi testimonium, in cuius scira (diocesi) sit, quod penitentiam acceperit.

[Be mansworum.] Ond se ðe manað swerige, ⁊ hit him on open wurþe, ðæt he næfre eft aðwyrþe ne sy, ne binnon nanum gehalgodum lictune ne licge, þeah he forðfore, buton he hæbbe ðæs biscopes gewitnesse, ðe he on his scriftscire sy, þæt he hit swa gebet hæbbe, swa him his scrift scrife.

Und wer Meineid schwört, und [wenn] das über ihn offenbar wird: dass der nimmer wieder eideswürdig sei, noch, wenn er stirbt, innerhalb eines geweihten Friedhofes liege, ausser wenn er des Bischofes Zeugniss hat, in dessen Beichtsprengel er ist, dass er es so gebüsst habe, wie ihm sein Beichtvater Poenitenz auferlegt.

And whoever swears a false oath, and [if] that becomes manifest against him: that he never again be oath-worthy, nor, when he dies, lie within any consecrated graveyard, unless he has the witness of the bishop in whose confessional district he is, that he has made amends for it as his confessor prescribed for him.

And if anyone swears a false oath and it becomes manifest he has done so, he shall never again have the right to swear an oath; and he shall not be buried in any consecrated burial ground when he dies, unless he has the testimony of the bishop, in whose diocese he is, that he has made such amends as his confessor has prescribed to him.

And he who swears a false oath, and it becomes known against him, is never afterwards to be entitled to an oath, nor is he to be buried in a consecrated cemetery when he dies, unless he has the witness of the bishop in whose diocese he is that he has done penance for it as his confessor has prescribed for him.
div.note: I Em 6; II Cn 36; II Cn 36.1

note.label: contrast (harsher)
note.quote: those who swore false oaths were to be denied Christian burial — whereas Edward the Elder had merely denied perjurers any future oath-worthiness (above, p. 289)

Ich halte 26. 26, 1 zwar für archetyp an dieser Stelle, aber doch für einen Nachgedanken des Gesetzgebers. — Vgl. Gl Meineid 10. 11 b. Dieser Satz wird benutzt von II Cn 36, der jedoch Handabhauen androht

I consider 26. 26, 1 to belong to the archetype at this point, but nevertheless to be an afterthought of the lawgiver. — Cf. Gl Meineid 10. 11 b. This clause is used by II Cn 36, which, however, threatens cutting off the hand
Ehrenstrafe Meineidiger auch bei anderen Germanen; Wilda 524; s. Gl Grab 2 a
A penalty of dishonour for perjurers is found among other Germanic peoples too; Wilda 524; see Gl Grab 2 a

Die Kirche würde die Übertragung in ehrliches Grab (s. d. 3 a) anzuordnen haben. Gibt der Staat schon, wie deutlich II Cn 36, 1, dem Geistlichen Gericht (s. d. Gl 14 a) auch die Macht, gegen blosse Pönitenz (die doch jeder nicht Eidesfähige leicht einging) den Meineidigen wieder eidesfähig (s. d. Gl 6) zu machen? Oder betrifft die Ausnahme nur die Bestattung? Für erstere Deutung spräche, dass zum Begräbnis allein zwar wír nicht den Toten als Subjekt des Zeugnis-Empfangs nennen würden; aber der Agsa. konnte das wohl; s. Gl Tote 1 ff. Für die zweite Deutung spricht 26, 1, wenn meine Übs. zutrifft

It would be for the Church to order the transfer to an honourable grave (see that word 3 a). Does the State already give the ecclesiastical court (see that word in Gl 14 a), as clearly in II Cn 36, 1, the power also to make the perjurer competent to swear (see that word in Gl 6) again in return for mere penance (which, after all, anyone not competent to swear would readily undertake)? Or does the exception concern only the burial? In favour of the former interpretation would be the fact that, while we would not name the dead man as the subject receiving the testimony if burial alone were meant, the Anglo-Saxon probably could; see Gl Tote 1 ff. In favour of the second interpretation is 26, 1, if my translation is correct
